```{r setup}
library(lstrrr)
```

Here, we will compare the performance of `lstrrr` and `purrr`.

```{r}
setwd(usethis::proj_path())

files <- list.files(all.files = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
files_list <- dir_listwise(files)
```

```{r}
slow_string_op <- function(x, n = 10) {
  stopifnot(is.character(x))

  out <- x

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    out <- paste0(
      rev(strsplit(out, "", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]),
      collapse = ""
    )
    out <- toupper(out)
    out <- tolower(out)
  }

  out
}


bench <- microbenchmark::microbenchmark(
  purrr = {
    purrr::map(files, \(x) slow_string_op(x))
  },
  lstrrr = {
    list_map(files_list, \(x) slow_string_op(x))
  },
  purrr_pb = {
    purrr::map(files, \(x) slow_string_op(x), .progress = TRUE)
  },
  lstrrr_pb = {
    list_map(files_list, \(x) slow_string_op(x), .progress = TRUE)
  }
)
print(bench)
```


```{r}
ggplot2::autoplot(bench)
```
